[SWS_CM_00129] Ensuring the existence of SetHandler
Upstream requirements:
RS_CM_00218
⌈
Upon a call to
OfferService()
in a skeleton implementation for a given service,
the following error check shall be made: if for at least one contained
Field
having
hasSetter
=
true
no
SetHandler
(see [SWS_CM_00116]) has been registered
yet, the error code
ComErrc::kFieldSetHandlerNotSet
shall be returned in the
result type of
OfferService()
.
⌋
[SWS_CM_00826] Minimum send interval time monitoring for SetHandlers calls
by the client
⌈
To protect receivers from flooding/overload, each
Set()
of the respec-
tive field class shall have a configurable Minimum Send Interval (see
ServiceInter-
faceDeploymentElement
.
minimumSendInterval
), which specifies the minimum
amount of time that shall pass between two consecutive calls of SetHandlers by the
client, i.e., the minimum send interval limits the maximum Tx frequency of a given
Set()
call for a Field in the network. If the application tries to
Field::Set()
a field
value, by invoking
Set()
of the respective field class,
ara::com
shall check, whether
the time since the last successful handover of the
Set()
call the underlying transmis-
sion layer is greater than the specified Minimum Send Interval, i.e., the Minimum Send
Interval is not violated. If the
Set()
handler has never been invoked before, this shall
also successfully pass the minimum send interval check. If the Minimum Send Interval
is not violated,
ara::com
shall process the
Field::Set()
call by handing it over
to the transmission layer. The time of handover shall count as start of the new min-
imum send interval monitoring. If the Minimum Send Interval is violated,
ara::com
shall discard the
Field::Set()
call, and return the error code
ComErrc::kMini-
mumSendIntervalViolationError
